claims.text: The dynamic mechanical response of Co-free FeNiCrMn is controlled by a strain-rate- and temperature-dependent transition between deformation twinning and dislocation slip.
Removing cobalt produces local fluctuations in stacking-fault energy in FeNiCrMn.
Local stacking-fault-energy fluctuations determine whether accumulated dislocations nucleate twins or remain slip-dominated.
Deformation twinning enhances work hardening and ductility.
The proposed competition between twinning and slip maintains the strength-ductility balance of Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn has a predominantly FCC structure.
Solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn exhibits nanoscale compositional inhomogeneities.
Nanoscale chemical and stacking-fault-energy variations act as barriers or promoters for twin nucleation.
At lower strain rates and/or lower temperatures, reduced thermal activation favors dislocation pile-up.
Dislocation pile-up under lower-rate and/or lower-temperature conditions promotes deformation-twin nucleation.
Twin formation increases work hardening and ductility under lower-rate and/or lower-temperature conditions.
Higher strain rates and/or elevated temperatures enhance dynamic recovery and dislocation mobility.
Enhanced recovery and dislocation mobility suppress twinning and shift deformation toward dislocation slip.
Twin density will decrease and slip-dominated deformation will increase as strain rate and temperature increase.
Changing strain rate and temperature will shift yield strength, work-hardening rate, and serrated-flow behavior.
At room temperature and moderate strain rate, FeNiCrMn exhibits mixed dislocation slip and a noticeable fraction of deformation twins.
Significant secondary phases or substantial post-processing-induced microstructural refinement may change the proposed mechanism.
Dynamic recrystallization may influence mechanical performance under extreme conditions.
